common_name: Little Vision in Purple Astilbe (Dwarf Raspberry-Purple Chinese Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; this dwarf Walters Gardens introduction (USPP21855P2) is the darkest-flowered member of the Little Vision series and keeps its compact scale in the front of a shaded border.

directions: A dwarf sport within the chinensis Vision breeding line, Little Vision in Purple produces dense, finely cut bronze-green foliage topped by raspberry-purple plumes that read noticeably deeper than the pink-toned Little Vision selections. Its tight, compact habit and improved sun and drought tolerance relative to arendsii hybrids make it a reliable edger or container astilbe. Keep soil consistently moist through summer and divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring.

common_name: Spotlight Astilbe (Dark-Foliage Light Pink Chinese Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; the near-black young foliage of this Dutch-bred (van Veen) selection provides contrast well before the pink plumes open.

directions: Spotlight is distinguished by deep, near-black developing foliage that matures to a dark bronze-green, setting off numerous light pink flower panicles over a long midsummer bloom window. The narrowly upright, strong habit holds its plumes well above the foliage without flopping. Site it in reliably moist, humus-rich soil where the dark leaf color can be appreciated against lighter-leaved shade companions, and divide every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Flamingo was bred from Astilbe japonica 'Vesuvius' crossed with 'Bressingham Beauty' and inherits vigorous, uniform flowering.

directions: Flamingo is a vigorous Dutch arendsii-group hybrid bearing branched panicles of lightly fragrant pink flowers held well above glossy dark green, compound foliage. It flowers very freely and evenly across the clump, making a fuller-looking stand than many older arendsii cultivars of similar height. Grow in a streamside bed or shaded border with steady moisture, and divide crowded clumps every three to four years in spring.

common_name: White Wings Astilbe (Pink-Tinged White Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; a cross of 'Hennie Graafland' crossed with 'Weisse Gloria', both already common arendsii parents, bred by Wim van Veen in the Netherlands.

directions: White Wings carries neat, glossy dark green foliage and compact plumes of small white flowers that open with a faint pink blush before fading to cream, remaining shapely into autumn. It is a durable, free-flowering compact cultivar suited to the front of a shaded bed or mixed container planting. Keep the shallow crown consistently moist and mulched through summer heat, since dry soil quickly scorches the foliage.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; bred from 'Weisse Gloria' crossed with chinensis 'Vision in Pink', so it bridges the arendsii and Vision breeding lines.

directions: Vision Inferno produces exceptionally dense, large terminal panicles — reportedly thousands of individual florets per plume — in a soft white ground lightly blushed with pink, set against foliage that opens reddish-bronze before maturing to a strong dark green. Its broadly upright, sturdy habit holds the heavy flower heads above the foliage without staking. Give it steady moisture in a woodland-edge or pondside bed, and divide every three to four years once flowering slows.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; part of Dutch breeder Jan Verschoor's compact Younique series, siblings of the already-common Younique Salmon and Younique Carmine.

directions: Younique Raspberry forms a tidy, low mound of lacy green foliage topped by broad, triangular, lightly fragrant plumes in a saturated raspberry-red-purple, deeper and more intense than most arendsii pinks. Bred as an arendsii-japonica cross for strong, uniform rebloom on a compact frame, it performs well in containers as well as ground beds. Water regularly through summer and divide every few years to keep the clump tight and floriferous.

common_name: Younique Ruby Red Astilbe (Compact Fuchsia-Red Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; another Jan Verschoor Younique-series introduction (US Plant Patent USPP23143P2), distinct from the already-present Younique Salmon, Silvery Pink, and Carmine selections.

directions: Younique Ruby Red carries shorter but intensely saturated plumes in a vivid ruby-red with fuchsia overtones, among the most vibrant colors in the Younique line. The compact, mounding habit and strong, durable foliage make it well suited to small shaded beds, edging, and mixed containers where its color can stand out at close range. Provide steady moisture and divide the clump every three to four years to maintain dense flowering.

common_name: Younique Lilac Astilbe (Compact Dark Lilac-Pink Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a Jan Verschoor Younique-series selection (US Plant Patent USPP19847P2) grown for its unusually cool-toned lilac-pink plumes.

directions: Younique Lilac offers dark lilac-pink plumes over the same compact, lacy-leaved mound shared by the rest of the Younique series, giving the line a cooler-toned color option alongside its reds, salmons, and carmines. Its small stature and even flowering suit shaded rock gardens, edging, and container combinations as readily as open beds. Keep soil consistently moist and divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a 2004 Hans van de Meer (Netherlands) selection grown as much for its coppery-bronze spring foliage as for its flowers.

directions: Cappuccino emerges with glossy, coppery-bronze compound foliage that deepens through the season while dark purple-red stems carry up white flower plumes just above the foliage plane. The combination of colorful foliage, dark stems, and abundant white bloom gives it a longer season of interest than many single-trait astilbes. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil with some morning sun to intensify the foliage color, and divide every three to four years in spring.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a complex Hans van der Meer hybrid (japonica x arendsii crossed with thunbergii) discovered in 2015 and bred for a taller, later-season display.

directions: Moccachino is a vigorous, broadly upright hybrid combining japonica, arendsii, and thunbergii ancestry, producing large conical panicles of pure white flowers on strong reddish-tinted stems well above a dense, dark green mound of foliage. Its taller stature and good garden performance make it useful toward the back of a shaded border or as a specimen beside a pond. Provide consistent moisture through summer and divide crowded clumps every few years in spring.

common_name: Lowlands Ruby Red Astilbe (Tall Dark Red-Purple Chinese Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a tall Hans van der Meer (Compass Plants BV) selection in the Lowlands trade series, grown under the breeder code 'Harvandermeerrubyred'.

directions: Lowlands Ruby Red is a tall, vigorous chinensis-type astilbe carrying dark red-purple plumes on strong, upright stems well above a broad, mounding base of dark green foliage. Its height and sturdy stems make it a good back-of-border or cut-flower astilbe, blooming continuously over a long stretch of late spring into summer. Keep soil consistently moist and divide every three to four years once the clump becomes congested.

common_name: Lowlands White Astilbe (Tall Fragrant White Chinese Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; the white-flowered companion to Lowlands Ruby Red from the same Hans van der Meer breeding program.

directions: Lowlands White produces tall, conical panicles densely packed with pure white, sweetly fragrant flowers on strong upright stems rising well above dark green foliage. The scent is more noticeable than in most astilbe cultivars, making it a good choice near a seating area or path through a shaded border. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil and divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring.

common_name: Smile At Me Astilbe (Dwarf Dark Pink Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a Tom de Bruijn (Netherlands) dwarf introduction (US Plant Patent USPP28461P3) bred to be shorter and bushier than the older 'Gloria'.

directions: Smile At Me is a true dwarf arendsii astilbe, its broadly conical dark pink flower panicles rising just a few inches above a compact, dark green foliage mound on distinctive reddish-brown stems. Bred to be noticeably shorter and more floriferous than the long-standard 'Gloria', it fits well in small shaded beds, rock gardens, and containers where taller astilbes would overwhelm the space. Keep the shallow root zone consistently moist and divide every few years to maintain density.

common_name: Wonderful Day Astilbe (Bright Pink Reblooming Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; one of Dutch breeder Harrie Verduin's compact 'Day' series (US Plant Patent USPP32890P2), alongside Lovely Day, Happy Day, Lucky Day, and Sunny Day.

directions: Wonderful Day bears fluffy plumes of bright pink flowers on green stems over a compact, well-branched mound, blooming for several weeks from early summer with sporadic rebloom into late summer. As one of the newer Day-series astilbes it is bred for a tidy, uniform habit that performs reliably in containers as well as garden beds. Provide steady moisture through the growing season and divide clumps every three to four years in spring.

common_name: Lovely Day Astilbe (Light Pink Bronze-Edged Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a Harrie Verduin Day-series selection grown for boldly divided, bronze-edged dark green foliage beneath its flower plumes.

directions: Lovely Day produces fluffed, light pink flower panicles over deeply divided dark green leaves that often carry a bronze edge, giving the foliage its own ornamental presence even before bloom. Like its Day-series siblings it keeps a compact, well-balanced habit suited to small beds and mixed containers. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade and divide every three to four years to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Happy Day Astilbe (Snow-White Compact Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; the white-flowered member of Harrie Verduin's Day series (US Plant Patent USPP32866P2).

directions: Happy Day carries copious plumes of snow-white, feathery flowers over a compact, evenly proportioned mound of dark green foliage, blooming through June and July. Its bright color and tidy scale make it a strong contrast plant next to the darker pinks and reds of other Day-series or arendsii astilbes. Keep soil consistently moist through the growing season and divide every three to four years in early spring.

common_name: Lucky Day Astilbe (Dark Pink Compact Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in organically rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade; bred by Harrie Verduin from a 2013 cross made in Heemskerk, Netherlands.

directions: Lucky Day blooms heavily with dark pink flower plumes on a compact plant, standing somewhat taller than most of its Day-series siblings while keeping a tidy, dense habit. It suits shady borders among trees and shrubs, where its saturated flower color stands out against greener companions. Provide organically rich, consistently moist soil and divide the clump every three to four years once flowering begins to thin.

common_name: Sunny Day Astilbe (Red-Flowered Drought-Tolerant Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to morning sun; a Harrie Verduin Day-series selection (US Plant Patent USPP32916P2) noted for above-average sun and drought tolerance.

directions: Sunny Day bears fluffed plumes of red flowers over boldly divided, dark green foliage sometimes edged in bronze, and tolerates more sun and drier soil than most astilbe cultivars once established. It still performs best with regular watering but is a useful choice for the sunnier, drier edge of a shaded bed. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep flowering strong.

common_name: Perfect Day Astilbe (Dwarf Dark Pink-Purple Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; a Harrie Verduin (Compass Plants BV) dwarf introduction (US Plant Patent USPP32900P2) bred for dense, upright flowering on a compact frame.

directions: Perfect Day forms a dense, bushy mound of dark green foliage from which strong, tall peduncles carry dark pink-and-purple flower panicles studded with tens of thousands of tiny blooms per plant over the season. Its vigorous but compact habit gives outsized flower presence relative to its modest footprint. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade, and divide every three to four years as the clump fills in.
